chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother, from his father, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recite: 'And they were shaken violently, then they were shaken violently, so that the Messenger said.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الرَّسُولُ: The Messenger (referring to Prophet Muhammad or a prophet)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recite the verse of Zalzalah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s (as) pedagogical use of *tajwid* and vocal emphasis to convey the eschatological magnitude of the earth's upheaval described in Surah Az-Zalzalah. By repeating 'zuzilū', the Imam underscores the visceral reality of the Day of Judgment, linking the physical shaking of the earth to the spiritual reckoning where even prophets feel the weight of divine justice. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of using recitation as a means to internalize Quranic themes, connecting the cosmic event to the human experience of accountability.
